expect:
Which one of the following is the best example of a closed skill?
A) A football player receiving a through pass from a teammate
B) A gymnast performing a cartwheel on the floor exercise mat
C) A hockey player hitting a moving ball past a goalkeeper
D) A basketball player taking a free throw during a fast break
value:
Which one of the following is the best example of a closed skill?
A) A football player receiving a through pass from a teammate
B) A gymnast performing a cartwheel on the floor exercise mat
C) A hockey player hitting a moving ball past a goalkeeper
D) A netball player intercepting a pass during a match
note: F1: a basketball free throw is a closed skill, so option D was a second correct answer and contradicted this lesson's own 4-mark question. The replacement distractor is a genuine open skill, which also makes the existing mark scheme true.

find: as this is the most frequently penalised mistake.
replace: as this is the term the specification itself uses.
note: F2: removes an invented claim about how often examiners penalise 'achievable' and replaces it with the real reason to learn 'accepted'.

find: Mo Farah described being able to sense the precise moment his running economy started to drop in the final 200 m of a 5,000 m race.
replace: an elite distance runner can sense the exact moment their stride loses efficiency in the final 200 m of a 5,000 m race.
note: F3: removes an invented statement attributed to a named real athlete. The teaching point about elite intrinsic feedback is kept.

find: too much causes over-performance through anxiety
replace: too much causes poor performance through anxiety
note: F5: over-arousal lowers performance. 'Over-performance' contradicted the inverted-U curve taught in the same lesson.

find: When Beth Mead scored a hat-trick in England’s opening game of the 2022 UEFA Women’s Euros
replace: When Beth Mead scored a hat-trick against Norway at the 2022 UEFA Women’s Euros
note: F6: Mead scored one goal in the opening game against Austria. Her hat-trick came against Norway on 11 July 2022.

find: Dame Sarah Storey’s 17 Paralympic gold medals
replace: Dame Sarah Storey’s 19 Paralympic gold medals
note: F7: Storey has 19 Paralympic golds after Paris 2024. The figure 17 was correct only to Tokyo 2020.

find: One-sided answers are capped at the Developing band.
replace: A one-sided answer leaves out half of what the question asks.
note: F9: removes an invented capping rule. The advice to write both sides is kept.

find: A response that only condemns PED use without engaging with the arguments athletes make for using them will be capped at the Developing band.
replace: A response that only condemns PED use, and never engages with the arguments athletes make for using them, is not a balanced answer.
note: F10: removes an invented capping rule while keeping the point about balance.

expect: Describe two side effects of blood doping for a performer.
value: Describe three side effects of blood doping for a performer.
note: F11: the 3-mark tariff, the mark scheme and the model answer all expect three side effects.
F12: index 2 is 'A rule giving the home team extra time in finals'. The correct option is index 1, 'The benefit gained from playing in a familiar venue with crowd support'.

find: a concept explored in the inverted-U theory covered in Lesson 10
replace: a concept explored in the inverted-U theory covered earlier in this unit
note: F13: the inverted-U theory is Lesson 6, not Lesson 10. A lesson-number-free reference stays correct if the order changes.

find: Mental (serotonin, stress, emotional control) and social (teamwork, cooperation, socialisation) benefits carry equal mark-scheme weight.
replace: Mental (serotonin, stress, emotional control) and social (teamwork, cooperation, socialisation) benefits matter just as much.
note: F14: removes an invented mark-scheme weighting while keeping the point that all three dimensions must be covered.

expect: Mark schemes award equal weight to physical, mental and social benefits — ignoring one loses marks.
value: A wellbeing question covers all three dimensions, so leaving one out answers only part of it.
note: F15: same invented weighting claim, memorised through a flashcard. The replacement is 16 words and is not a list.

find: Elite distance runners such as Dina Asher-Smith prepare for competition partly by ensuring glycogen stores are fully loaded through carbohydrate-rich meals in the days before an event.
replace: Elite marathon runners prepare for competition partly by ensuring glycogen stores are fully loaded through carbohydrate-rich meals in the days before an event.
note: F16: Dina Asher-Smith is a 100 m and 200 m sprinter, not a distance runner, and carbohydrate loading over several days is an endurance practice.

find: For a sprint cyclist like Geraint Thomas
replace: For a road cyclist like Geraint Thomas
note: F17: Geraint Thomas is a road and stage-race cyclist; his track event was the team pursuit, not sprint cycling.
